description: Netlify deployment configuration, security headers, and serverless health function
steps: Rewrite netlify.toml with full build config (NODE_VERSION=22, PNPM_VERSION=10), SPA redirect, security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), and cache headers for /assets/*, /*.js, /*.css
Create netlify/functions/health.ts - a Netlify serverless function returning JSON health status with timestamp

Create public/_headers file with security headers including Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com, font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com, img-src 'self' data: https:, connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co wss://*.supabase.co https://api.openai.com https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com)
acceptance_criteria: netlify.toml has build command, publish dir, NODE_VERSION, PNPM_VERSION, SPA redirect, security headers, and cache headers for static assets
netlify/functions/health.ts exports a handler that returns 200 JSON response
public/_headers contains CSP and all security headers
verification: Run pnpm build to confirm build still works with netlify.toml present
Verify netlify.toml is valid TOML syntax
findings: Build passes cleanly. TOML validated. _headers file correctly copied to dist/ during build. netlify/functions/health.ts uses @netlify/functions types (not installed as dep, but this is expected for Netlify build environment).
